newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Solid Energy to barge coal to Australia.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Solid Energy to barge coal to Australia.

text.p: Solid Energy, the former Coal Corporation of New Zealand, on Wednesday confirmed plans to barge coal to Australia from Westport from the middle of June.

Solid Energy international general manager Geoff Hipkins said the company had entered into a four year contract with Ocean Bulk Services, a joint venture between Union Shipping and Ocean Towing Salvage to export coal to Port Kembla in Australia, directly from Westport using a large barge and a tug.
A barge was enroute from the U.S. and would arrive in the middle of next month and a newly purchased tug was also enroute and expected to arrive at the same time.
Solid Energy national service manager John Ryan said the coal to be barged had a low profit margin and it was not sustainable to ship it through the Port of Lyttelton, near Christchurch.

The coal that will be barged is currently shipped through Lyttelton but the deal should have little effect on the port volumes because Solid Energy was increasing overall coal volumes in an export drive, Ryan said.
Port of Lyttelton is listed on the stock exchange.
Solid Energy currently ships about 1.5 million tonnes of coal through Lyttelton annually but expansion plans are expected to raise its exports to four million tonnes.
Solid Energy has been trying to extract a commitment from the port to expand its facilities and has separately been querying rail charges.
